body:
There is a problem with exposing this method as is. It depends on `get_viewport()->is_input_handled()`, which is a state that changes depending on when this is called.

Calling `call_gui_input` would only work as expected if it is called after a `push_input` and before an event is accepted, but exposing it means it can be called from anywhere.
If you do call this after an event has been accepted *anywhere* in the current viewport, only the signal will be emitted, which will lead to differences in behavior with controls that use the virtual call or c++ `gui_input` instead.
This also prevents `call_gui_input` from working when called multiple times in a row.

And it can't easily be removed since a control will expect that accepting the event in the `gui_input` signal will stop it from going to the virtual method. So the accept event / `is_input_handled` has to know somehow if it is being set for the regular input propagation, or for this call. I don't know if that is possible reliably since they can be called at anytime.

I completely agree with the assessment of kitbdev and think that exposing this function is a bad idea. Calling `Control::_call_gui_input` not only executes the wanted functionality, but also has side-effects with other input handling aspects, its interaction with input_handled being one of them. If it wouldn't break compatibility, personally I would even go so far as to unexpose `Viewport::push_input`, because conceptually it suffers from the same problems. Basically we would need to separate the input system (covering all aspects of the internal system how input is handled) from the action system (the actions, that an input event causes). However, because `Viewport::set_input_handled` is exposed to GDScript, that function can be called in any action. We would need to find a way to move the call of set_input_handled (red) to the blue area in the above graphic. That would allow us to call the action without any interference with the input system. I believe, that there are also other hooks into the input system, which would also need to be addressed.
